items.evidence: Recursion happens when a function calls itself inside its own body
items.note: The student correctly defined recursion as a function calling itself.

items.evidence: you always need a base case
items.note: The student stated that a recursive function requires a base case.

items.evidence: so the function knows when to finally stop calling itself and return a value
items.note: The student explained that the base case stops further calls and returns a value.

items.evidence: break down a large problem into smaller subproblems
items.note: The student mentioned smaller subproblems but did not state that each recursive call must operate on a strictly smaller subproblem.
The student did not mention call stack frames.
The student did not mention stack overflow errors.
The student did not discuss rewriting recursion iteratively.
The student did not mention tail call optimization.

target_reason: Understanding how problems shrink on each call is essential for preventing infinite loops.
target_focus: how the problems get smaller with each call
